name: React.js & Next.js Development
headline: React 19 & Next.js Architecture Solutions
description: In-depth technical guides, React 19 compiler optimization, Server Actions, streaming SSR, and Next.js App Router design patterns for scalable web apps.

faqs.q: What are the main performance benefits of React 19?
faqs.a: React 19 introduces the automatic React Compiler (React Forget), removing manual useMemo and useCallback hooks while enabling streamed HTML boundaries and Server Actions for single-digit millisecond latency.

faqs.q: How does Next.js App Router improve SEO?
faqs.a: Next.js App Router renders Server Components by default, sending lightweight HTML directly to search crawlers without client-side rendering delays.

name: Modern JavaScript (ES2026)
headline: ECMAScript 2026 & Clean Architecture Patterns
description: Master state-of-the-art ES2026 features including explicit resource management, array grouping, microtask event loops, and clean modular code standards.

faqs.q: What is explicit resource management in ES2026?
faqs.a: ES2026 introduces the top-level 'using' statement for automatic resource cleanup of event listeners, WebSockets, and database cursors upon exiting block scope.

name: SharePoint Framework (SPFx)
headline: Enterprise SPFx & Microsoft 365 Web Parts

faqs.q: How do you secure SPFx web parts with Microsoft Entra ID?
faqs.a: SPFx leverages AadHttpClient and MSGraphClient to acquire OAuth tokens transparently from modern SharePoint sessions.

name: Web Performance & Core Web Vitals
headline: Crushing INP & Sub-1.2s LCP Score Guidelines
description: Actionable engineering strategies for eliminating Interaction to Next Paint (INP) latency, zero CLS layouts, and 100/100 Lighthouse performance scores.

faqs.q: How do you optimize Interaction to Next Paint (INP)?
faqs.a: Break long tasks into microtasks using scheduler.yield() or offload heavy UI calculations to web workers to keep main threads responsive.

name: AI & Gemini Model Integration
headline: Full-Stack Generative AI Integration
description: Architecting low-latency AI applications using Google Gemini API, streaming Server-Sent Events, function calling, and structured JSON schemas.

faqs.q: How do you stream LLM outputs to frontend UIs?
faqs.a: Use Server-Sent Events (SSE) or Fetch API readable streams to render text tokens progressively as they generate.

name: CSS Subgrid & Modern Layouts
headline: CSS Subgrid, Container Queries & Design Systems
description: Pixel-perfect multi-column layouts using CSS Subgrid, container query breakpoints, fluid clamp() typography, and accessible UI token design.

faqs.q: Why use CSS Subgrid over regular CSS Grid?
faqs.a: CSS Subgrid enables nested child elements to align directly to parent track lines, ensuring card titles and footers stay perfectly aligned across rows.

name: TypeScript 5.5 Enterprise
headline: Type Safety & Generics at Enterprise Scale
description: Leveraging TypeScript 5.5 inferred type predicates, isolated declarations, template literal types, and strict null check architecture.

faqs.q: What is type predicate inference in TypeScript 5.5?
faqs.a: TypeScript 5.5 automatically infers return type predicates for functions returning booleans, eliminating manual 'x is Type' assertions.

name: Web Accessibility (WCAG 2.2)
headline: WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance & Accessible UI Systems
description: Building universally accessible web interfaces with screen reader ARIA roles, focus traps, keyboard navigation, and high contrast design standards.

faqs.q: What is the minimum contrast ratio for WCAG 2.2 AA text?
faqs.a: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal body text and 3:1 for large typography and essential UI graphics.
